message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I'm p1 with $186 and an orange monopoly at two houses each. I just paid $18 rent to p2, who has only $25 cash and owns several mortgaged properties.

I'm checking the cash figures for accuracy. I paid $18 rent, so my balance should be $186. I'm unsure why p2's state shows only $25.

I'll trust the stated cash figures. p2 has $25. p3 has $2901 and owns all four railroads plus a pink monopoly with four houses each.

p4 is bankrupt. p3 acquired NC, Park Place, and Boardwalk for $0. p3 now controls dark blue and green properties too. I am in serious trouble. My orange monopoly cannot survive four-house pink rent. I must choose between ending my turn or proposing a trade.

I will not build houses or unmortgage utilities. Indiana is mortgaged to block p2's red monopoly. I will keep the orange set intact. Selling six houses returns $300, but $186 cash is below the rebuild threshold.

Building houses would be suicidal. Four-house pink rent is $625 to $700. I have no buffer against that.

Orange two-house rent is $200 to $220 per property. p3 has $2901, so this does not threaten them. p2 is nearly bankrupt with only $25 cash. The game is effectively a one-on-one battle between me and p3.

I could build one house on a single orange property for $100. That would raise rent from $200 to $550. But I would have only $86 left. p3 owns all four railroads. A $200 railroad rent would bankrupt me.

I mapped the board positions from Kentucky. Rolling a 3 lands on Indiana, which is mortgaged and worth nothing. Rolling a 4 lands on Illinois, owned by p3 with no houses and only $20 rent. I am calculating how many of these rolls would bankrupt me.

Rolling a 5 on the B&O Railroad would cost $200. That is $14 short of my $186 balance, so I would need to sell a house to survive. All other rolls from Kentucky are safe.

I cannot build houses now. Three houses on the orange set would cost $300, and I only have $186. One house costs $100 and leaves $86. That is too little cash to survive a B&O Railroad hit.

Uneven house counts are legal, so a 3-2-2 spread is allowed. I am now calculating landing probabilities for p3 to assess whether the rent increase justifies the risk.

I mapped the full board positions. p3 is on Community Chest, but the state lists the position as "COMMUNITY_CHEST" without specifying which of the three spaces. I am on Kentucky (space 21). p3 is clearly winning.

I am on Kentucky. The pink properties sit just after jail at spaces 11, 13, and 14. I must avoid them entirely. p2 is stuck on Virginia with only $25 cash. He has not moved since turn 124.

p2 is likely bankrupting to p3's pink set. If that happens, p3 would gain Kentucky and Ventnor. I still hold Indiana, which blocks the red monopoly. I am now considering a trade with p3.

I rejected trading Indiana to p3. They already own Illinois, and p2 still holds Kentucky. I cannot afford to give up that mortgage block.

I considered trading with p2 for Kentucky, but that would not complete a red monopoly since p3 still owns Illinois. I will not offer cash to p2.

I will not sell houses. Even zero houses on the orange set still yields double rent, but that is too weak to threaten p3. I have no debt to force a sale. Unmortgaging Indiana costs $121.

Unmortgaging Indiana would leave $65 cash, but the base rent is only $18 and I lack the red monopoly to double it. Unmortgaging both utilities would cost $166 and leave just $20. Neither option is worth the cost.

I am now reconsidering trading Indiana to p3. They still need Kentucky from p2, so they might pay a large sum for it. That cash could let me survive or build houses. I will not unmortgage utilities.

If p2 goes bankrupt to p3, p3 would inherit Kentucky. Indiana is the only remaining barrier to a red monopoly. I will not trade it.
